name: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd
title: Jain Irrigation Systems Ltd - 500219 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Jain Irrigation Q2 FY27 revenue rose over 10% to about INR 1,576 crore, EBITDA INR 207 crore, and working capital cycle fell to 179 days.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a good quarter: revenue grew above 10% to about INR 1,576 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 207 crore, with margin at about 13.2% versus 13.9% a year earlier. Adjusted PAT after NCD wind-down effects was about INR 40 crore, and H1 revenue was about INR 3,100 crore (up about 4%) with H1 EBITDA of INR 372 crore. Cash conversion was strong, with about INR 206 crore of the INR 208 crore EBITDA converted to cash, used to repay INR 230 crore of NCDs. Management flagged a severe monsoon deficit in west and south India and high polymer prices as ongoing headwinds, and guided H2 to roughly flattish year-on-year.

financial_highlights.value: INR 207 crore (also cited as INR 208 crore)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after NCD wind-down adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: down from 183 days in Q1 and 205 days at end Sep 2025
government-linked about INR 1,200 crore (project INR 800 crore, MIP INR 400 crore)

segments.name: Hi-Tech MI (micro-irrigation) and tissue culture
segments.commentary: Margin about 18.8%; growth in high-teens; combined retail business grew about 12% and domestic revenue about 10% after a chosen reduction in project business.

segments.name: Piping
segments.commentary: Was down 25-30% in Q1; Q2 roughly flat YoY. Management expects FY27 piping growth of 8-10% on large-diameter and non-agri demand; weakness is concentrated in rural agri markets.

segments.name: Agro-processing (food, beverages)
segments.commentary: About INR 560 crore in Q2, up about 8.4%; margin about 12%. Phase two beverage line work started.

segments.name: Plastics (incl. overseas sheet business)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 17%; margin about 9%. Medium-term target about 12%.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be roughly flattish YoY given drought; management will comment on January for any improvement.
Possible H2 upside if polymer prices ease between December and March and deferred farmer purchases return.
Net receivable reduction of at least INR 300 crore by March 2027, mainly government project and MIP receivables.
Expected inflows in H2: Maharashtra incentive about INR 100 crore and land monetisation about INR 100-150 crore.
Interest saving of about INR 20 crore per year in FY28 after repaying the 0% NCDs; standalone interest cost about INR 50 crore per quarter.

Growth capex: tomato JV about INR 30-40 crore by March quarter (subject to asset acquisition closing in December); beverage phase two about INR 100 crore between March and June quarters; biochar growth capex mainly in FY28.
capex_capacity: Tomato JV: INR 30-40 crore expected in the March quarter, contingent on asset acquisition closing by December.
Beverage phase two: about INR 100 crore, with spend between March and June quarters; work has already started.
Biochar: proof-of-concept stage; major growth capex expected in FY28; carbon credits and field trials in progress.
Management aims for higher capacity utilisation in FY28 but did not quantify capacity or utilisation levels.
demand_pricing: Monsoon described as the worst in about 35 years nationally and over 50 years in Maharashtra; west and south (80-85% of business) most affected; Kharif hit and Rabi likely hit.
High polymer (resin) prices from the West Asia conflict and uncertain supply led farmers to defer purchases; management expects a demand booster if prices ease.

Management let go about INR 200-250 crore of business in H1: about INR 100 crore of micro-irrigation in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, and about INR 150 crore of solar water pump business, due to slow cash collection.
Project business: 78 projects at start, 7-8 active now, 15-20 closed in the last six months; project revenue about INR 14 crore in Q2 and about INR 30-33 crore in H1.
Coffee tissue culture: orders received from Coffee Board; coffee still small versus banana and pomegranate.

qa_highlights.question: Why has piping not grown while peers have, and will it turn around?
qa_highlights.answer: Piping is sold mainly into rural agriculture, while peers sell more into urban plumbing and drainage. Management expects FY27 piping growth of 8-10%, driven by non-agri applications in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much government receivable will be collected by March?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about INR 800 crore project and INR 400 crore MIP receivables, management expects a net reduction of at least INR 300 crore by March, with no write-off expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much business was let go in H1 due to liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 200-250 crore: about INR 100 crore of micro-irrigation in southern states and about INR 150 crore of solar water pump business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 FY27 outlook versus last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least flattish H2 revenue; upside depends on polymer price relief and monsoon, with January giving more visibility.

qa_highlights.question: What are the interest savings for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 20 crore per year, because the INR 800 crore repaid this year is 0% NCD debt; standalone interest cost stays about INR 50 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold when polymer prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is based on average inventory cost, so no negative lag is expected; medium-term targets are Plastics about 12% and Hi-Tech MI 18-19%, with 1-2% upside from fixed-cost absorption.

risks_watch: Severe drought in west and south India (Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu), with Rabi likely affected and some areas with water curtailed for drinking.
Polymer price and supply volatility from the West Asia conflict, and its effect on Plastics and piping margins.
Repayment of about INR 450-500 crore of debt, with the second tranche due in March 2027; dependence on receivable collections and H2 incentive and land inflows.
Recovery of legacy government project and MIP receivables; management expects these to be cleared over the next few quarters, with project business at zero by FY28.
Pricing discipline in rural markets: management has let go business where cash collection was slow.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q2 operating and cash metrics, but cautious on the outlook: management was hesitant to commit to H2 growth beyond flattish and cited drought, polymer costs and the March debt repayment as the key watch items.
key_quotes: Out of INR 208 crore of EBITDA, almost INR 206 crore have been converted into cash.
I think we will, with whatever I know and I can see, I think at least we will remain flattish.
We would expect these to be reduced on a net basis at least by INR 300 crore plus between now and March.
we don't expect write-off from receivables.

adds.what: Tomato JV asset acquisition (INR 30-40 crore capex, contingent on acquisition closing in December)
Beverage phase two line in agro-processing (about INR 100 crore capex)

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue at least flattish YoY given drought and high polymer prices, with no quantified capacity or order book behind recovery; growth backing is limited to small capex (tomato JV, beverage phase two) and possible demand recovery if polymer prices ease.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin about 13.2% vs 13.9% a year earlier and H1 at 12.1%; medium-term targets are Plastics about 12% (from ~9%) and Hi-Tech MI 18-19% (held at ~18.8%), with 1-2% upside from fixed-cost absorption only if volumes recover.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No quantified capacity or utilisation was given; the only adds are a tomato JV (INR 30-40 crore, March quarter) and beverage phase two (about INR 100 crore, March-June quarters), and biochar major growth capex is pushed to FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 FY27 revenue guided at least flattish YoY after H1 revenue up only about 4% to INR 3,100 crore, with monsoon the worst in about 35 years and INR 200-250 crore of business let go in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and management only aims for higher utilisation in FY28; the known capex (tomato JV, beverage phase two, biochar growth capex in FY28) is already committed, so a fresh major announcement is not clearly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management will comment in January on any H2 improvement; upside depends on polymer prices easing between December and March and deferred farmer purchases returning.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 revenue guidance already cut to at least flattish YoY amid the worst monsoon in about 35 years and high polymer prices, with Rabi likely hit and second NCD tranche of INR 450-500 crore debt repayment due March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Only capacity adds like beverage phase two and coffee tissue culture orders are mentioned; no new product launch with a date was discussed.

rows.label: Receivable reduction of at least INR 300 crore by March 2027
rows.why: Management expects a net reduction of at least INR 300 crore in government project and MIP receivables (about INR 1,200 crore government-linked of INR 1,860 crore standalone), with no write-off expected, and the cycle already fell to 179 days from 205 days a year ago.

rows.label: Interest saving of about INR 20 crore per year in FY28
rows.why: INR 800 crore of 0% NCD debt repaid this year yields about INR 20 crore annual interest saving, though standalone interest cost stays about INR 50 crore per quarter until then.

rows.label: Maharashtra incentive and land monetisation inflows in H2
rows.why: Expected inflows of about INR 100 crore Maharashtra incentive and INR 100-150 crore land monetisation are needed to cover the INR 450-500 crore debt repayment due March 2027.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 operating and cash metrics (INR 206 crore of INR 208 crore EBITDA converted to cash, cycle down to 179 days) but cautious on H2, guiding only to at least flattish and citing drought, polymer costs and the March debt repayment; analysts pressed on why piping lagged peer
